claim: Less than 50% of hippocampal CA1 presynaptic boutons contain mitochondria.
source: Surprisingly, less than 50% of hippocampal CA1 presynaptic boutons contain mitochondria, raising the question of whether synapses without mitochondria can sustain changes in efficacy.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work (Shepherd and Harris, 1998; Kang et al., 2008; Pathak et al., 2015; Chavan et al., 2015) as referenced in the Introduction.

claim: Mitochondria support synaptic transmission through production of ATP, sequestration of calcium, synthesis of glutamate, and other vital functions.
source: Mitochondria support synaptic transmission through production of ATP, sequestration of calcium, synthesis of glutamate, and other vital functions.
evidence: This is a general statement drawing from established scientific knowledge about mitochondrial functions in neurons.

claim: At 30 and 120 min after TBS-LTP, vesicles were decreased only in presynaptic boutons that contained mitochondria at P15.
source: At 30 and 120 min after TBS-LTP, vesicles were decreased only in presynaptic boutons that contained mitochondria at P15, and vesicle decrement was greatest in adult boutons containing mitochondria.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, specifically in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: Vesicle decrement was greatest in adult boutons containing mitochondria.
source: At 30 and 120 min after TBS-LTP, vesicles were decreased only in presynaptic boutons that contained mitochondria at P15, and vesicle decrement was greatest in adult boutons containing mitochondria.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, specifically in Figure 8.

claim: Presynaptic mitochondrial cristae were widened, suggesting a sustained energy demand.
source: Presynaptic mitochondrial cristae were widened, suggesting a sustained energy demand.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations in Figure 10 and is interpreted based on prior knowledge about mitochondrial ultrastructure and energy demand.

claim: Mitochondrial proximity reflected enhanced vesicle mobilization well after potentiation reached asymptote.
source: Thus, mitochondrial proximity reflected enhanced vesicle mobilization well after potentiation reached asymptote, in parallel with the apparently silent addition of new dendritic spines at P15 or the silent enlargement of synapses in adults.
evidence: This is an interpretive claim based on the experimental data showing vesicle changes in mitochondria-containing boutons at 30 and 120 min after TBS.

claim: Mitochondria produce more than 90% of all neuronal ATP.
source: They produce more than 90% of all neuronal ATP (Harris et al., 2012), which is needed in many steps of the synaptic vesicle cycle (Südhof, 1995; Chua et al., 2010; Sudhof and Rizo, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Harris et al., 2012.

claim: ATP is needed in many steps of the synaptic vesicle cycle.
source: They produce more than 90% of all neuronal ATP (Harris et al., 2012), which is needed in many steps of the synaptic vesicle cycle (Südhof, 1995; Chua et al., 2010; Sudhof and Rizo, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Südhof, 1995; Chua et al., 2010; Sudhof and Rizo, 2011.

claim: Mitochondria synthesize the excitatory neurotransmitter glutamate from glutamine.
source: Mitochondria synthesize the excitatory neurotransmitter glutamate from glutamine (Waagepetersoen et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Waagepetersoen et al., 2003.

claim: The filling of synaptic vesicles with glutamate requires mitochondrial ATP.
source: The filling of synaptic vesicles with glutamate requires mitochondrial ATP (Forgac, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Forgac, 2007.

claim: Docking of synaptic vesicles does not appear to require ATP.
source: Docking of synaptic vesicles does not appear to require ATP; however, priming them for subsequent release is an ATP-dependent process (Yao and Bajjalieh, 2008; Verhage and Sørensen, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Yao and Bajjalieh, 2008; Verhage and Sørensen, 2008.

claim: Priming synaptic vesicles for subsequent release is an ATP-dependent process.
source: Docking of synaptic vesicles does not appear to require ATP; however, priming them for subsequent release is an ATP-dependent process (Yao and Bajjalieh, 2008; Verhage and Sørensen, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Yao and Bajjalieh, 2008; Verhage and Sørensen, 2008.

claim: Dissociation of the SNARE complex is an ATP-dependent process that reactivates monomeric SNARE proteins.
source: Following release, dissociation of the SNARE (soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment protein receptor) complex is an ATP-dependent process that reactivates monomeric SNARE proteins (Sudhof and Rizo, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Sudhof and Rizo, 2011.

claim: Endosome-based recycling of synaptic vesicles causes local depletion of ATP and increased production of ATP by mitochondria.
source: Endosome-based recycling of synaptic vesicles causes local depletion of ATP and increased production of ATP by mitochondria (Rangaraju et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Rangaraju et al., 2014.

claim: The proteome of presynaptic mitochondria is enriched in proteins that supply energy and are engaged in synaptic transmission.
source: Mitochondria contain their own DNA; the proteome of presynaptic mitochondria is enriched in proteins that supply energy and are engaged in synaptic transmission, whereas the proteome of nonsynaptic axonal mitochondria clusters around metabolic and morphogenic proteins (Völgyi et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Völgyi et al., 2015.

claim: The proteome of nonsynaptic axonal mitochondria clusters around metabolic and morphogenic proteins.
source: Mitochondria contain their own DNA; the proteome of presynaptic mitochondria is enriched in proteins that supply energy and are engaged in synaptic transmission, whereas the proteome of nonsynaptic axonal mitochondria clusters around metabolic and morphogenic proteins (Völgyi et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Völgyi et al., 2015.

claim: Axonal mitochondria typically remain stationary for periods of hours even after substantial activation.
source: Axonal mitochondria can move, although they typically remain stationary for periods of hours even after substantial activation (Overly et al., 1996; Kang et al., 2008; Obashi and Okabe, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Overly et al., 1996; Kang et al., 2008; Obashi and Okabe, 2013.

claim: Diffusion of ATP from mitochondria-containing boutons can sustain synaptic transmission at cultured hippocampal synapses without mitochondria.
source: Interestingly, diffusion of ATP from mitochondria-containing boutons can sustain synaptic transmission at cultured hippocampal synapses without mitochondria (Pathak et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pathak et al., 2015.

claim: ATP from glycolysis can support synaptic transmission under resting conditions.
source: In addition, ATP from glycolysis can also support synaptic transmission under resting conditions, but mobilization of vesicles from the reserve pool requires mitochondrial ATP (Verstreken et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Verstreken et al., 2005.

claim: Mobilization of vesicles from the reserve pool requires mitochondrial ATP.
source: In addition, ATP from glycolysis can also support synaptic transmission under resting conditions, but mobilization of vesicles from the reserve pool requires mitochondrial ATP (Verstreken et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Verstreken et al., 2005.

claim: Total vesicular release correlates well with the presence and volume of presynaptic mitochondria.
source: Indeed, total vesicular release correlates well with the presence and volume of presynaptic mitochondria, suggesting their proximity may enhance synaptic transmission (Sun et al., 2013; Ivannikov et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Sun et al., 2013; Ivannikov et al., 2013.

claim: Prior to weaning, at postnatal day 21 in rats, neurons have a low capacity for glucose utilization and instead use ketone bodies as their primary energy substrate.
source: Prior to weaning, at postnatal day 21 in rats, neurons have a low capacity for glucose utilization and instead use ketone bodies as their primary energy substrate (Vannucci, 1994; Nehlig et al., 1988; Nehlig, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Vannucci, 1994; Nehlig et al., 1988; Nehlig, 2004.

claim: Ketone body metabolism requires mitochondria.
source: Unlike glucose metabolism, ketone body metabolism requires mitochondria (Fukao et al., 2004), suggesting there might be a stronger requirement for mitochondria to fuel synaptic vesicle cycling at younger ages.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fukao et al., 2004.

claim: There might be a stronger requirement for mitochondria to fuel synaptic vesicle cycling at younger ages.
source: Unlike glucose metabolism, ketone body metabolism requires mitochondria (Fukao et al., 2004), suggesting there might be a stronger requirement for mitochondria to fuel synaptic vesicle cycling at younger ages.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the inference from ketone body metabolism requirements.

claim: Changes in mitochondrial dimensions and the ultrastructure of matrix and cristae reflect altered energy demands.
source: Changes in mitochondrial dimensions and the ultrastructure of matrix and cristae reflect altered energy demands (Ishihara et al., 2009; Cagalinec et al., 2013; Hackenbrock, 1966, 1968; Perkins et al., 2010; Packer, 1960).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ishihara et al., 2009; Cagalinec et al., 2013; Hackenbrock, 1966, 1968; Perkins et al., 2010; Packer, 1960.

claim: Under resting conditions, mitochondria have loosely packed matrix and narrow cristae.
source: Under resting conditions, mitochondria have loosely packed matrix and narrow cristae, whereas under conditions of high energy demand the matrix compacts and cristae widen (Hackenbrock, 1966, 1968).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hackenbrock, 1966, 1968.

claim: Under conditions of high energy demand the matrix compacts and cristae widen.
source: Under resting conditions, mitochondria have loosely packed matrix and narrow cristae, whereas under conditions of high energy demand the matrix compacts and cristae widen (Hackenbrock, 1966, 1968).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hackenbrock, 1966, 1968.

claim: Mitochondria provide local sequestration of calcium that is important for enhanced vesicular release during post-tetanic potentiation lasting a few minutes.
source: Mitochondria also provide local sequestration of calcium that is important for enhanced vesicular release during post-tetanic potentiation lasting a few minutes (Tang and Zucker, 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tang and Zucker, 1997.

claim: Fewer than half of hippocampal presynaptic boutons contain a mitochondrion.
source: Given their many critical functions, it was surprising to find that fewer than half of hippocampal presynaptic boutons contain a mitochondrion (Shepherd and Harris, 1998; Kang et al., 2008; Pathak et al., 2015; Chavan et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Shepherd and Harris, 1998; Kang et al., 2008; Pathak et al., 2015; Chavan et al., 2015.

claim: LTP produces enhancement of synaptic efficacy lasting hours to days or longer.
source: LTP is a cellular model of learning that produces enhancement of synaptic efficacy lasting hours to days or longer.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about LTP.

claim: Prior work has shown an LTP-related increase in synapse number at P15.
source: Prior work has shown an LTP-related increase in synapse number at P15 (Watson et al., 2016), whereas, in the young adults, synapses enlarged at the expense of synaptogenesis by 120 min after the induction of LTP with TBS (Bourne and Harris, 2011; Bell et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Watson et al., 2016.

claim: In young adults, synapses enlarged at the expense of synaptogenesis by 120 min after the induction of LTP with TBS.
source: Prior work has shown an LTP-related increase in synapse number at P15 (Watson et al., 2016), whereas, in the young adults, synapses enlarged at the expense of synaptogenesis by 120 min after the induction of LTP with TBS (Bourne and Harris, 2011; Bell et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bourne and Harris, 2011; Bell et al., 2014.

claim: At P15, control stimulation resulted in fewer dendritic spines, whereas LTP resulted in more spines than in perfusion-fixed hippocampus.
source: At P15, control stimulation resulted in fewer dendritic spines, whereas LTP resulted in more spines than in perfusion-fixed hippocampus (Figure 2A, from Watson et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A and cited from Watson et al., 2016.

claim: At P15, single synapse boutons were significantly reduced under control stimulation relative to perfusion-fixed.
source: At P15, single synapse boutons were significantly reduced under control stimulation relative to perfusion-fixed (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The frequency of nonsynaptic boutons did not increase under control stimulation at P15.
source: It is unlikely that these spines simply retracted, leaving intact presynaptic boutons, because the frequency of nonsynaptic boutons did not increase (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2E and is used to support an inference.

claim: The frequency of single synaptic boutons in the LTP condition was comparable to the perfusion-fixed and greater than in the control condition at P15.
source: The frequency of single synaptic boutons in the LTP condition was comparable to the perfusion-fixed and greater than in the control condition, whereas multisynaptic boutons increased above control and perfusion-fixed conditions (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Multisynaptic boutons increased above control and perfusion-fixed conditions at P15 following LTP.
source: The frequency of single synaptic boutons in the LTP condition was comparable to the perfusion-fixed and greater than in the control condition, whereas multisynaptic boutons increased above control and perfusion-fixed conditions (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: At P15, the new spines formed after the induction of LTP made synapses primarily with pre-existing axonal boutons.
source: These findings suggest that at P15 the new spines formed after the induction of LTP made synapses primarily with pre-existing axonal boutons.
evidence: This is an interpretive claim based on the data showing changes in bouton frequencies.

claim: About 75% of the presynaptic boutons were SSBs but only 25% of those contained mitochondria at P15 in perfusion-fixed hippocampus.
source: About 75% of the presynaptic boutons were SSBs but only 25% of those contained mitochondria, whereas 25% were multisynaptic boutons and more than half (59%) of those contained mitochondria (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: About 25% of presynaptic boutons were multisynaptic boutons and more than half (59%) of those contained mitochondria at P15 in perfusion-fixed hippocampus.
source: About 75% of the presynaptic boutons were SSBs but only 25% of those contained mitochondria, whereas 25% were multisynaptic boutons and more than half (59%) of those contained mitochondria (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Individual PSD areas were larger when presynaptic boutons contained a mitochondrion at P15.
source: Individual PSD areas were larger when presynaptic boutons contained a mitochondrion, although this effect did not reach statistical significance for multisynaptic boutons (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: At P15, both single synaptic boutons and multisynaptic boutons had more docked vesicles when they contained a mitochondrion.
source: At P15, both single synaptic boutons and multisynaptic boutons had more docked (Figure 3E) and nondocked (Figure 3F) vesicles when they contained a mitochondrion.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: At P15, both single synaptic boutons and multisynaptic boutons had more nondocked vesicles when they contained a mitochondrion.
source: At P15, both single synaptic boutons and multisynaptic boutons had more docked (Figure 3E) and nondocked (Figure 3F) vesicles when they contained a mitochondrion.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The portion of axonal volume occupied by mitochondria (28%) was markedly less than the portion of axonal volume without mitochondria (72%).
source: First, we computed that the portion of axonal volume occupied by mitochondria (28%) was markedly less than the portion of axonal volume without mitochondria (72%, Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Mitochondria were equally distributed between nonsynaptic inter-bouton regions (51%) and synaptic boutons (49%).
source: Next, we showed that mitochondria were equally distributed between nonsynaptic inter-bouton regions (51%) and synaptic boutons (49%, Figure 3H).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Axonal diameters were significantly wider at synaptic boutons (0.41 ± 0.015 µm) than at nonsynaptic regions (0.32 ± 0.008 µm).
source: As predicted, we found that axonal diameters were significantly wider at synaptic boutons (0.41 ± 0.015 µm) than at nonsynaptic regions (0.32 ± 0.008 µm, n = 75, F1,71 = 37.5, p<0.001).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of measured data.

claim: Mitochondrial diameters were similar at synaptic (0.24 ± 0.009 µm) and nonsynaptic (0.23 ± 0.007 µm) regions.
source: However, mitochondrial diameters were similar at synaptic (0.24 ± 0.009 µm) and nonsynaptic (0.23 ± 0.007 µm) regions (n = 75, F1,71 = 1.25, p=0.27).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of measured data.

claim: For nondocked and docked vesicles as well as PSD areas, the distance threshold was ~3 µm.
source: For nondocked and docked vesicles as well as PSD areas, the distance threshold was ~3 µm (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by piecewise regression analysis shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: At P15, approximately a third of the boutons from perfusion-fixed hippocampus had synapses in each categorical range, with 33% containing mitochondria, 31% having Dm ≤ 3, and 36% having Dm > 3.
source: At P15, approximately a third of the boutons from perfusion-fixed hippocampus had synapses in each categorical range, with 33% containing mitochondria, 31% having Dm ≤ 3, and 36% having Dm > 3.
evidence: This claim is supported by data analysis of mitochondrial distances.

claim: Boutons containing a mitochondrion had more nondocked vesicles than those with Dm ≤ 3 µm, which were greater than those with Dm > 3 µm.
source: Boutons containing a mitochondrion had more nondocked vesicles (Figure 4D), docked vesicles (Figure 4E), and larger total PSD areas (Figure 4F) than those with Dm ≤ 3 µm, which were all greater than those with Dm > 3 µm.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Boutons containing a mitochondrion had more docked vesicles than those with Dm ≤ 3 µm, which were greater than those with Dm > 3 µm.
source: Boutons containing a mitochondrion had more nondocked vesicles (Figure 4D), docked vesicles (Figure 4E), and larger total PSD areas (Figure 4F) than those with Dm ≤ 3 µm, which were all greater than those with Dm > 3 µm.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Boutons containing a mitochondrion had larger total PSD areas than those with Dm ≤ 3 µm, which were greater than those with Dm > 3 µm.
source: Boutons containing a mitochondrion had more nondocked vesicles (Figure 4D), docked vesicles (Figure 4E), and larger total PSD areas (Figure 4F) than those with Dm ≤ 3 µm, which were all greater than those with Dm > 3 µm.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: About 25–42% of the synapses had presynaptic mitochondria located within the three categories of proximity at P15.
source: About 25–42% of the synapses had presynaptic mitochondria located within the three categories of proximity (Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The proportions of synapses with mitochondria in different proximity categories were unchanged relative to perfusion-fixed levels under control conditions at P15.
source: These proportions were unchanged relative to perfusion-fixed levels under control conditions (χ2(6) = 5.35, p=0.5) and did not differ significantly at any time after TBS.
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of the data.

claim: Neither docked nor nondocked vesicle numbers differed significantly between control stimulation and perfusion-fixed conditions at any time point or mitochondrial proximity at P15.
source: Neither docked nor nondocked vesicle numbers differed significantly between control stimulation and perfusion-fixed conditions at any time point or mitochondrial proximity (Figure 6, compare blue to gray bars).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: At 5 min after TBS at P15, there were no significant effects of TBS on docked or nondocked vesicle numbers regardless of mitochondrial proximity.
source: At 5 min (Figure 6A), there were no significant effects of TBS on docked or nondocked vesicle numbers regardless of mitochondrial proximity (Figure 6A1 and A2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: At 30 min after TBS at P15, the boutons with mitochondria had fewer docked vesicles per synapse than in time-matched control or perfusion-fixed conditions.
source: At 30 min (Figure 6B), the boutons with mitochondria had fewer docked vesicles per synapse than in time-matched control or perfusion-fixed conditions (Figure 6B1), but the nondocked reserve pool was unchanged (Figure 6B2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6B1.

claim: At 30 min after TBS at P15, the nondocked reserve pool was unchanged in boutons with mitochondria.
source: At 30 min (Figure 6B), the boutons with mitochondria had fewer docked vesicles per synapse than in time-matched control or perfusion-fixed conditions (Figure 6B1), but the nondocked reserve pool was unchanged (Figure 6B2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6B2.

claim: At 120 min after TBS at P15, there were fewer docked vesicles at synapses with presynaptic mitochondria or Dm ≤ 3 µm in the TBS relative to the control or perfusion-fixed conditions.
source: At 120 min (Figure 6C), there were fewer docked vesicles at synapses with presynaptic mitochondria or Dm ≤ 3 µm in the TBS relative to the control or perfusion-fixed conditions (Figure 6C1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6C1.

claim: At 120 min after TBS at P15, the reserve pool of nondocked vesicles was diminished in the TBS relative to the control or perfusion-fixed conditions when the presynaptic boutons contained a mitochondrion.
source: In contrast with earlier time points, the reserve pool of nondocked vesicles was also diminished at 120 min in the TBS relative to the control or perfusion-fixed conditions when the presynaptic boutons contained a mitochondrion (Figure 6C2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6C2.

claim: When a mitochondrion was present in the presynaptic bouton at P15, the number of docked and nondocked vesicles was significantly decreased across synapses of all sizes at both 30 min and 120 min following the induction of LTP relative to control stimulation.
source: When a mitochondrion was present in the presynaptic bouton, the number of docked and nondocked vesicles was significantly decreased across synapses of all sizes at both 30 min (Figure 7A,B) and 120 min (Figure 7E,F) following the induction of LTP relative to control stimulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7A, B, E, F.

claim: When no mitochondrion was present in the presynaptic bouton at P15, neither docked nor nondocked vesicle numbers differed significantly between TBS and control conditions at 30 min or 120 min.
source: When no mitochondrion was present in the presynaptic bouton, neither docked nor nondocked vesicle numbers differed significantly between TBS and control conditions at 30 min (Figure 7C,D) or 120 min (Figure 7G,H).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7C, D, G, H.

claim: At 120 min, the total number of boutons per cubic micron was about 50% less in the TBS relative to control conditions in adults.
source: At 120 min, the total number of boutons per cubic micron was about 50% less in the TBS relative to control conditions (Figure 8C, Bourne et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 8C and cited from Bourne et al., 2013.

claim: More of the presynaptic boutons contained mitochondria in adults than at P15 for both control and TBS conditions.
source: Additionally, more of the presynaptic boutons contained mitochondria in adults than at P15 for both control (χ2 = 14.3, df = 1, p<0.001) and TBS conditions (χ2 = 33.7, df = 1, p<0.00001; compare Figure 8D,E with Figure 5 at 120 min).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical comparison of data shown in Figure 8D, E and Figure 5.

claim: In adults, presynaptic boutons with a mitochondrion had more vesicles than those without a mitochondrion.
source: In the adults, like P15, presynaptic boutons with a mitochondrion had more vesicles than those without a mitochondrion (Figure 8F1, G1; F2,226 = 47.2, p<0.001).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 8F1, G1.

claim: In adults, the PSD areas of synapses were larger when their presynaptic boutons contained a mitochondrion (0.074 ± 0.0058 µm2) than when they did not contain a mitochondrion (0.040 ± 0.0025 µm2).
source: Like P15, the PSD areas of the adult synapses were larger when their presynaptic boutons contained a mitochondrion (0.074 ± 0.0058 µm2) than when they did not contain a mitochondrion (0.040 ± 0.0025 µm2; F2,226 = 26.3, p<0.0001).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of measured data.

claim: In adults, there was a marked decrease in vesicle numbers of mitochondria-containing boutons across synapses of all sizes at 120 min after TBS relative to control stimulation.
source: Furthermore, there was a marked decrease in vesicle numbers of mitochondria-containing boutons across synapses of all sizes at 120 min after TBS relative to control stimulation in adults (Figures 8F2 and 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 8F2 and F3.

claim: In adults, there was a small decrease in vesicle number in boutons without a presynaptic mitochondrion at 120 min after TBS.
source: However, there was also a small decrease in vesicle number in boutons without a presynaptic mitochondrion in adults (Figures 8G2 and 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 8G2 and G3.

claim: Mitochondrial volume was reduced at P15 and increased in adults in the TBS versus control conditions at 120 min.
source: Mitochondrial volume was reduced at P15 and increased in adults in the TBS versus control conditions (Figure 9C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Mitochondrial diameters did not differ significantly between the TBS and control conditions for either age, although they were slightly wider in the adults than at P15.
source: Mitochondrial diameters did not differ significantly between the TBS and control conditions for either age, although they were slightly wider in the adults than at P15 (Figure 9D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 9D.

claim: Mitochondrial lengths were shorter in the control than in the TBS condition at P15 but were longer in the control condition in adults.
source: Mitochondrial lengths were shorter in the control than in the TBS condition at P15 but were longer in the control condition in adults (Figure 9E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 9E.

claim: The frequency of mitochondria was greater in adults than at P15 under control conditions, but was much less in the adults after TBS.
source: The frequency of mitochondria was greater in adults than at P15 under control conditions, but was much less in the adults after TBS (Figure 9F).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 9F.

claim: At P15, less than 50% of all mitochondria were synaptic (i.e. located within the presynaptic bouton).
source: At P15, less than 50% of all mitochondria were synaptic (i.e. located within the presynaptic bouton), whereas in the adults more than 80% of all mitochondria were synaptic (Figure 10B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 10B.

claim: In adults, more than 80% of all mitochondria were synaptic.
source: At P15, less than 50% of all mitochondria were synaptic (i.e. located within the presynaptic bouton), whereas in the adults more than 80% of all mitochondria were synaptic (Figure 10B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 10B.

claim: Under control stimulation conditions, more than 70% of axonal mitochondria were in the orthodox configuration in both P15 and adult axons.
source: Under control stimulation conditions, more than 70% of axonal mitochondria were in the orthodox configuration in both P15 and adult axons (Figure 10C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 10C.

claim: The frequency of mitochondria in the orthodox configuration decreased by about half at 120 min post-TBS in both P15 and adult slices relative to control stimulation.
source: The frequency of mitochondria in the orthodox configuration decreased by about half at 120 min post-TBS in both P15 and adult slices relative to control stimulation and were replaced by dramatic increases in mitochondria with the condensed, intermediate, and mixed configurations (Figure 10D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 10D.

claim: The LTP-related shifts in mitochondrial configurations resulted in wider cristae at both synaptic and nonsynaptic mitochondria for the TBS vs. control conditions at both ages.
source: The LTP-related shifts in mitochondrial configurations resulted in wider cristae at both synaptic and nonsynaptic mitochondria for the TBS vs. control conditions at both ages (Figure 10E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 10E.

claim: Changes in mitochondria structure are consistent with an elevated demand for presynaptic ATP at 120 min after TBS-LTP.
source: These changes in mitochondria structure are consistent with an elevated demand for presynaptic ATP at 120 min after TBS-LTP.
evidence: This is an interpretive claim based on the observed changes in mitochondrial ultrastructure and established knowledge about mitochondrial function.

claim: At P15, less than 30% of the presynaptic boutons contained mitochondria at 2 hr following TBS.
source: At P15, less than 30% of the presynaptic boutons contained mitochondria at 2 hr following TBS, suggesting that TBS-related spinogenesis mostly involved presynaptic boutons without mitochondria.
evidence: This claim is based on data analysis and is used to support an inference.

claim: TBS-related spinogenesis at P15 mostly involved presynaptic boutons without mitochondria.
source: At P15, less than 30% of the presynaptic boutons contained mitochondria at 2 hr following TBS, suggesting that TBS-related spinogenesis mostly involved presynaptic boutons without mitochondria.
evidence: This is an interpretive claim based on the data showing mitochondrial distribution.

claim: At P15, the TBS-related spinogenesis likely occurred at boutons lacking enhanced vesicle mobilization.
source: Since only the mitochondria-containing boutons had elevated vesicle mobilization at P15, the TBS-related spinogenesis likely occurred at boutons lacking enhanced vesicle mobilization.
evidence: This is an interpretive claim based on the data showing vesicle changes only in mitochondria-containing boutons.

claim: In adults, the TBS-related synapse enlargement and vesicle mobilization occurred at boutons with or without mitochondria.
source: In adults, the TBS-related synapse enlargement and vesicle mobilization occurred at boutons with or without mitochondria.
evidence: This claim is based on data analysis from adult samples.

claim: In adults, much of the growth in the PSD involved the addition of nascent zones that had PSDs but lacked presynaptic vesicles.
source: However, much of the growth in the PSD involved the addition of nascent zones that had PSDs but lacked presynaptic vesicles, and hence were likely to be unresponsive to vesicular release (Bell et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bell et al., 2014.

claim: Nascent zones with PSDs but lacking presynaptic vesicles were likely to be unresponsive to vesicular release.
source: However, much of the growth in the PSD involved the addition of nascent zones that had PSDs but lacked presynaptic vesicles, and hence were likely to be unresponsive to vesicular release (Bell et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an interpretive claim based on the observation of nascent zones lacking vesicles.

claim: A decrease in the number of synaptic vesicles following LTP has been reported for nearly forty years.
source: Consistent with our findings, a decrease in the number of synaptic vesicles following LTP has been reported for nearly forty years (Applegate et al., 1987; Fifková and Van Harreveld, 1977; Lushnikova, et al., 2008; Bourne et al., 2013; Bayazitov et al., 2007; Stanton et al., 2005), although not in the context of presynaptic mitochondria, postsynaptic growth, or explicit comparison between immature and mature synapses as reported here.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple prior studies.

claim: Following induction of LTP, both evoked vesicle release probability and spontaneous miniature excitatory synaptic potentials have been reported to be increased.
